take_homes: Access and absorption are different. A rollout number tells me who got a licence, not who changed how they work.
Start from the colleague's actual job and ask what would have to be true for them to switch. Don't start from what I want to share.
A plan needs a people half with real names for who owns it, governs it and operates it. Without names it isn't a plan.

monday.move: Ask one of my HR business partners how she builds the weekly people-metrics summary today, what she trusts in it and what she'd need to see to use a draft from an agent. Build nothing before that.
monday.who: One HR business partner, the one who prepares the numbers for me
monday.stop_condition: If she says she wouldn't use it, or if the draft would need employee data that I haven't cleared yet, I stop and don't build anything.
monday.blocker: I haven't asked the works council or the DPO about employee data in an AI tool. I'll use aggregated numbers or invented data until I have.

misconception.why: The story shows the barrier was trust and decision-making, not the technology or headcount. It doesn't say roles won't go, and the module never answers my headcount question. I now think the headcount question depends on who absorbs the agents and who decides.

one_line: Good on why rollouts stall and on starting from a colleague's job. The repeated context paragraphs are filler, and I still don't have my headcount answer.
